Now let me understand the logic. Let me look at the logic.ts to understand handleMove, getFirstWellState, and mode transitions.

Now I understand the logic. Let me analyze the bug.

The bug: If you play a replay that doesn't end the game (for example, `D`), then the game will be stuck in replay mode even after there are no more inputs, forcing the user to refresh the page.

In `handleClickReplay`:
```js
const wellStateId = 0
replayTimeoutId = wellStateId in replay
  ? setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)
  : undefined
const mode = wellStateId in replay ? 'REPLAYING' : 'PLAYING'
```

So mode = 'REPLAYING' if wellStateId (0) in replay. If replay = ['D'], then 0 in replay → REPLAYING.

`handleReplayTimeout` is triggered after replayTimeout. It does:
```js
if (mode === 'REPLAYING') {
  await this.handleRedo()

  if (wellStateId + 1 in replay) {
    nextReplayTimeoutId = setTimeout(this.handleReplayTimeout, replayTimeout)
  }
}
```

So after handling redo, it only schedules the next timeout if `wellStateId + 1 in replay`. For replay = ['D'], wellStateId starts at 0. After redo, wellStateId becomes 1. `1 in ['D']`? Array `['D']` has index 0 only, so `1 in replay` is false. So no next timeout is scheduled. And mode remains 'REPLAYING'.

Wait, but the `setState` at the end:
```js
this.setState({
  replayTimeoutId: nextReplayTimeoutId
})
```
But `this.handleRedo` calls `this.handleMove` which does `setState`. So there are two setStates. The handleRedo's setState happens before. The handleReplayTimeout's setState sets replayTimeoutId.

So the state becomes: mode stays 'REPLAYING' (since handleMove sets nextMode = mode which is 'REPLAYING', unless game over). And no more timeouts are scheduled. So the game is stuck in 'REPLAYING' mode, showing "replaying..." and ignoring all key inputs (because handleLeft etc. only work in PLAYING mode).

That's the bug. The user can't do anything except refresh.

Now the fix: once the replay ends, we should switch to 'PLAYING' mode so the user can continue playing. Let me think about how.

Actually, let me re-read. The issue says "it should still probably allow the user to do something once the replay ends."

      {...props}
    />

  let user: ReturnType<typeof userEvent.setup>

  beforeEach(() => {
    user = userEvent.setup()
  })

  it('rejects a rotation system with no pieces', () => {
    const game = renderGame({
      rotationSystem: {
        placeNewPiece: () => ({ id: '', o: NaN, x: NaN, y: NaN }),
        rotations: {}
      }
    })
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('error-real').textContent, 'Have to have at least one piece!')

    game.unmount()
  })

  it('rejects a well depth below the bar', () => {
    const game = renderGame({ bar: 4, wellDepth: 3 })
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('error-real').textContent, 'Can\'t have well with depth 3 less than bar at 4')
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('error-interpretation').textContent, 'Caught this exception while trying to start HATETRIS. Application halted.')
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('rejects a well width less than 4', () => {
    const game = renderGame({ wellWidth: 3 })
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('error-real').textContent, 'Can\'t have well with width 3 less than 4')
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('error-interpretation').textContent, 'Caught this exception while trying to start HATETRIS. Application halted.')
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('ignores all keystrokes before the game has begun', async () => {
    const warn = sinon.stub(console, 'warn')
    const game = renderGame()
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('start-button').textContent, 'start new game')

    await user.keyboard('{Left}')
    await user.keyboard('{Right}')
    await user.keyboard('{Down}')
    await user.keyboard('{Up}')
    await user.keyboard('{Control>}z{/Control}')
    await user.keyboard('{Control>}y{/Control}')

    assert.equal(warn.getCalls().length, 6)
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('start-button').textContent, 'start new game')

    warn.restore()
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('lets you play a few moves', async () => {
    const warn = sinon.stub(console, 'warn')

    const game = renderGame()

    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('start-button'))
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 4)

    await user.keyboard('{Left}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 4)

    await user.keyboard('{Right}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 4)

    await user.keyboard('{Down}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 4)

    // Rotate, puts part of the piece in contact with the bar below
    await user.keyboard('{Up}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 3)
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--bar well__cell--live').length, 1)

    // Undo
    await user.keyboard('{Control>}z{/Control}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 4)

    // Redo
    await user.keyboard('{Control>}y{/Control}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 3)
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--bar well__cell--live').length, 1)

    // Warn on attempted redo at end of history
    await user.keyboard('{Control>}y{/Control}')
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--live').length, 3)
    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('well__cell well__cell--bar well__cell--live').length, 1)
    assert.equal(warn.getCalls().length, 1)

    warn.restore()
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('just lets you play if you enter an empty replay', async () => {
    const game = renderGame()

    const prompt = sinon.stub(window, 'prompt')
    prompt.returns('')
    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('replay-button'))

      ['Paste replay string...']
    ])
    prompt.restore()

    assert.equal(screen.queryAllByTestId('down').length, 1)
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('lets you select a different AI and play a full game with it and provides a replay which you can copy', async () => {
    let calls: any[] = []
    const clipboard = navigator.clipboard
    Object.defineProperty(navigator, 'clipboard', {
      value: {
        writeText: async (...args: any[]) => {
          calls.push(args)
        }
      },
      writable: true
    })

    const game = renderGame()

    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('select-ai'))
    await user.click(screen.queryAllByTestId('enemy')[2])
    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('start-button'))
    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('enemy-short').textContent, 'AI: ❤️')

    // "copied!" disappears after a while

    assert.equal(screen.getByTestId('copy-replay').textContent, 'copy replay')

    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('done'))
    game.unmount()
  })

  it('lets you use a custom AI', async () => {
    const game = renderGame()

    await user.click(screen.getByTestId('select-ai'))
